'''Russel E. Caflisch''' (born 29 April 1954)<ref name="vol2">{{cite book| editor1-last=Katle| editor1-first=Pamela M.| editor2-last=Nemeh| editor2-first=Katherine H.| editor3-last=Schusterbauer| editor3-first=Noah| chapter=Russel E. Caflisch| title=American Men & Women of Science| volume=2| year=2005| page=5| url=https://archive.org/details/americanmenwomen0002unse_m9n5/page/n5/mode/2up?q=caflisch| publisher=Thompson Gale| location=Detroit| isbn=978-1-4144-0462-2}}</ref> is an American mathematician.

==Biography==
Caflisch is a former Director of the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] at [[New York University]] (NYU), and a Professor in the Mathematics Department. Russel Edward Caflisch was born in [[Charleston, West Virginia]].<ref name="vol2" /> He received his bachelor's degree from Michigan State University in 1975. He earned a master's degree and Ph.D. in Mathematics from the Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences at New York University.<ref name="vol2" /> His dissertation was titled "The Fluid Dynamic Limit and Shocks for a Model Boltzmann Equation." (1978)<ref>{{cite thesis| url=https://www.proquest.com/openview/1c83b1a3c99711b37ebc62da156bb788/| title=The Fluid Dynamic Limit and Shocks for a Model Boltzmann Equation|id={{ProQuest| <!-- Insert ProQuest data here -->}}| first=Russel E.| last=Caflisch| publisher=New York University| degree=PhD| access-date=December 14, 2023}}</ref> He has also held faculty positions at Stanford and NYU. He has served as PhD advisor for 22 students, with 55 descendants.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.genealogy.ams.org/id.php?id=33190| title=Russel Caflisch| website=The Mathematics Genealogy Project| access-date=May 18, 2019}}</ref> Until August 2017, Caflisch was the director of the [[Institute for Pure and Applied Mathematics|Institute for Pure & Applied Mathematics (IPAM)]] and a professor in the Mathematics department, where he also held a joint appointment in the department of Materials Science and Engineering.<ref>{{cite web| title=IPAM Directors| url=http://www.ipam.ucla.edu/people/directors/| website=IPAM| date=21 January 2014| access-date=May 18, 2019}}</ref>

Caflisch was a founding member of [[California NanoSystems Institute]] (CNSI).  Caflisch's expertise includes topics in the field of applied mathematics, including [[partial differential equation]]s, [[fluid dynamics]], [[plasma physics]], [[materials science]], [[Quasi-Monte Carlo method|Monte Carlo methods]], and computational finance.

Caflisch served as Director of the Courant Institute until the end of his second term in May 2025. As of 2026, he serves as a Professor of Mathematics in the Courant Institute School of Mathematics, Computing, and Data Science.

==Recognition==
Caflisch was awarded the [[Hertz Foundation|Hertz Foundation Graduate Fellowship]] in 1975<ref>{{cite web|title=Hertz Foundation Fellows List|url=https://hertzfoundation.org/dx/fellows/fellows.aspx|access-date=May 18, 2019}}</ref> and a [[Sloan Fellowship|Sloan Foundation Research Fellowship]] in 1984. He was named a fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] in 2009,<ref>{{cite web|title=SIAM Fellows List|url=https://www.siam.org/Prizes-Recognition/Fellows-Program/All-SIAM-Fellows/Class-of-2009|access-date=May 18, 2019}}</ref> the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2012,<ref>{{cite web|title=AMS Fellows List|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list-institution|access-date=May 18, 2019}}</ref> and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2013.<ref>{{cite web|title=American Academy of Arts and Sciences Fellows List|url=http://www.ucla.edu/about/awards-and-honors/faculty/american-academy-of-arts-and-sciences|access-date=May 18, 2019}}</ref>
He was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in April 2019.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2019-nas-election.html| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190430143122/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2019-nas-election.html| url-status=dead| archive-date=April 30, 2019| title=2019 NAS Election| website=National Academy of Sciences| date=April 30, 2019| access-date=May 18, 2019}}</ref>

Caflisch was an invited speaker at [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Madrid]] in 2006,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sanz-Solé |first1=Marta |last2=Soria |first2=Javier |last3=Varona |first3=Juan L. |last4=Verdera |first4=Joan |date=2007-05-15 |title=International Congress of Mathematicians Madrid 2006 |url=https://ems.press/books/standalone/24 |access-date=2023-03-17 |website=ems.press |language=en}}</ref> and at the conference ''Dynamics, Equations and Applications'' in [[Kraków]] in 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=DEA 2019 Invited Speakers |url=https://www.dea.agh.edu.pl/invitedspeakers |access-date=2023-03-17}}</ref>

==Personal life==
His parents are Edward G. Caflisch and Dorothy G. Caflisch.

Russel Caflisch is married to Carol Lynn Meylan.
